newsitem.title: FRANCE: Court blames state in French river disaster.
newsitem.headline: Court blames state in French river disaster.

text.p: A French appeal court ruled on Tuesday that the state and a local council must compensate families for a 1987 disaster in which a flash flood caused by a rain-swollen river swept away a camping site, killing 21 people.

The Lyon administrative appeals court found that the state and the Grand-Bornand village council in the French Alps were legally responsible for the disaster because they had authorised construction of the site despite the risk of flooding and failed to mention previous floods in local planning documents.
The families of two people killed in the disaster had filed civil lawsuits against persons unknown for manslaughter by negligence but the local public prosecutor closed the case.

A defence committee then applied to the Grenoble administrative court for redress, but it dismissed the suit in 1994, upholding the government representative's argument that only fate was to blame for the tragedy.
However the government representative at the Lyon appeal acknowledged that the disaster had been "forseeable and not exceptional".
